To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) β-carotene and other yellow pigment(s) are more sensitive than chlorophyll a and b to SO 2 and HF; (2) chlorophyll a is more sensitive to HCl than chlorophyll b; (3) the sensitivity to SO 2 is in the order β-carotene, HCl, chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, HF.

the concentration of β- carotene in the chloroplast of the leaves of Acer platanoides L. is reduced by the action of SO 2, NO 2, O 3 and HF, and that the concentration of this pigment can be used to indicate the presence of air pollution.

(a) The concentration of chlorophill and β-carotene in leaves of the same plant varies with the position of the leaf in the plant; (b) The concentration of β-caroten in the leaves of the same tree is affected by air pollution, while that of chlorophyll is not; (c) The concentration of both chlorophyll and β-carotin in the same leaves decreases as the age of the leaf increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an analytical method which is based on changes in the concentration or the composition of plant pigments.
the development of a method for determining the concentration of β-Carotene by means of a spectrophotometric technique.
the effects on the pigment system of plants of air pollution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, as far as chlorophyll is concerned, the action of SO 2 is the most important.

the concentration of β - carotene is a sensitive indicator for the action of pollutants, and that the concentration of chloroplast pigments is a sensitive indicator of the action of pollutants on chloroplasts.

changes in the concentration or decomposition of pigments can only be used as an indication of the effects on plants of the action of air pollutants when the action of these pollutants on the pH-value is taken into consideration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it is not yet possible to develop a method of early recognition of the influence of air pollution by the study of pigment changes, and that the use of such a method is only justified in the case of β-carotenes.

the concentration of β -carotene and of the other yellow pigments is an indicator of the influence of air pollutants on plants, and that the concentration of chloroplasts is an indicator of their influence on the plants' metabolism.
the pigment analyses of plants are not suitable for the detection of the influence of air pollution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the data from the satellite to identify areas of high air pollution.
the effects of air pollutants on plants can be detected in the laboratory by measuring changes in chlorophyll concentration, which is the most sensitive indicator of the effects of pollutants.
we need to consider the impact of air pollution on the health of plants.
